title: Content Studio redesign: choose the visual world
question: Each sketch is the Reading passages editor with the TestNav exam as the default canvas and every existing control kept. Pick the world to build, or re-roll.

options.label: Ditto Master
options.thesis: The studio is the teacher's duplicating room: one violet ink runs the whole shell, and the white TestNav sheet is the print coming off it.
options.viewport: Violet navigation rail, a dense passage library, then the TestNav exam sheet on a pale desk; one ink rule under the title carries save state.
options.risk: A violet shell is a strong flavor to sit in for hour-long editing sessions.

raised.raise: Save state is carried by line form as well as color: solid rule for saved, dashed for unsaved changes, broken red for a failed save.
Every pane snaps to one 8px module and the layout reflows by whole columns, never by squeezing.
Library rows tighten to two lines so about fifteen passages are visible without scrolling.

options.label: Teacher's Edition
options.thesis: The student page sits in the middle exactly as students see it; everything a teacher adds lives in a margin beside it, in a second ink.
options.viewport: Top navigation bar, slim library column, TestNav exam page centered, and a teacher's margin on the right holding answer key, question tools, tags and publish state.
options.risk: A three-pane editor is the familiar arrangement; its distinction rests on the margin being executed precisely.

options.label: Divider Tabs
options.lineage: Tabbed reference binders with colored divider boards
options.thesis: Each workspace family owns one full-strength hue, and white working leaves sit on top of it, so you always know which section you are in.
options.viewport: A stepped tab rail down the right edge sized by how much each workspace holds; the English board in ultramarine behind white library and TestNav leaves.
options.case: Holds product clarity: tabs are familiar and location is unmistakable. Loses narrowly on identification, since a saturated board is louder than a tutor's desk.
options.risk: Full-strength color around the page can tire the eye if the gutters are not kept thin.

options.label: Graphite Bench
options.thesis: A graphite bench where panels tile and stay put, the white exam sheet is the only bright object, and Delete stands alone.
options.viewport: Slim header, text rail, library and inspector panels tiled around the lit TestNav sheet, and a status bar carrying save state.
options.case: Holds product clarity through persistent panels and isolated destructive actions. Loses on identification: it reads as a developer's tool more than a teacher's.
options.risk: A white exam page inside a dark shell is high contrast over long evening sessions.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.lineage: Glass spectrograms on a viewing box
options.thesis: State drawn as line height, dash and doubling on one calibrated rail.
options.viewport: Every workspace a tick on one off-centre rail, the open one blooming into a plate.
options.case: Loses both axes: hue-free status slows scanning a review queue, and tutors do not read spectrograms.
options.kept: Status readable by line form, not color alone.
options.risk: Unfamiliar status language on a working screen.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Importance as dot size on a coordinate field.
options.viewport: The content library as overlapping chart plates with an index.
options.case: Loses both axes: passages and questions are text to edit, not points to plot.
options.kept: An index whose entries point to an exact place.
options.risk: A map metaphor over a text editor.

options.label: Circle Catalog
options.thesis: Hundreds of coded cells packed edge to edge on one page.
options.viewport: The library as a wall of coded cells with a keyed map.
options.case: Loses both axes: passages have titles, not thumbnails, and the grid hides the editor.
options.kept: The courage to show many entries at once.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: A visible construction grid with monumental letterforms built on it.
options.viewport: Workspace names as giant grid-built letters over the tools.
options.case: Loses both axes: monumental type steals room from the exam page it should serve.
options.kept: One module governing every pane and reflow.
options.risk: Poster scale on a working screen.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A neutral white-and-grey authoring workbench with one blue accent, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Grey sidebar, library list, toolbar and the TestNav sheet: the current arrangement, tidied.
canonCard.risk: Closest to what the editor looks like today, so the change will feel smallest.
